t: Archaeological evidence places the carving between 2600 and 2500 BCE, for Khufu or his son Khafre, though no contemporary inscription names its maker.
Its body was cut from the quarry bedrock of the plateau, and the stone taken from around it built a temple in front that was never finished.
Drifting sand buried it again and again, and pharaohs, Roman officials and modern excavators cleared it in turn.
dyk: Its nose was not shot off by Napoleon's troops. The face shows marks of rods or chisels hammered in at the bridge and below the nostril, and the nose has been documented as damaged since at least the 10th century.
ev: The Sphinx is carved from the bedrock of the Giza Plateau for Khufu or Khafre
The young Thutmose IV digs out the front paws and sets up the Dream Stele between them
The Sphinx is cleared of sand in honour of Nero and a monumental stairway is built before its paws
A stela commemorates the restoration of the retaining walls around the Sphinx
According to al-Maqrizi, the Sufi Muhammad Sa'im al-Dahr defaces the Sphinx
The first modern archaeological dig, under Giovanni Battista Caviglia, uncovers the chest completely
Egyptian government engineers repair the head with a concrete collar after part of the headdress fell in 1926

f.made: Egyptians of the Old Kingdom, probably in the reign of Khufu or Khafre; whose face it shows (Khufu, Djedefre or Khafre) remains in dispute
f.form: A monolith carved from the limestone bedrock of the Mokattam Formation, 73 m long from paw to tail, 20 m high and 19 m wide at the rear haunches, facing east
f.where: On the Giza Plateau, on the west bank of the Nile in Giza, Egypt, part of the Memphite Necropolis World Heritage Site
f.known: the oldest known monumental sculpture in Egypt; a lion's body with a human head; the missing nose; the Dream Stele of Thutmose IV; centuries buried in sand; disputes over its date and likeness
